caveats: This is a fixed linear identity-gate surrogate, not contextual GELU or model inference.
Candidate sequences were frozen before corpus verification; no corpus-informed extractor retuning.
High-write-norm sources are selected independently per operator/checkpoint. Methods do not have matched source coverage.
Bounded paths often terminate before eight tokens. Compare eligibility and actual lengths, not only configured maxima.
Exact bigram-preserving shuffles are diagnostics, not uniformly sampled nulls or p-values.
The optional bias-GELU gate was implemented but was not run on real checkpoints in this recorded experiment.
conclusion: Retaining all signed MLP neuron contributions produces learned token associations but no evidence here of passage-specific sequence recovery beyond the bigram-preserving control.

limitations: Not uniform over Euler trails; not a p-value or calibrated null.
Only tests order beyond pairs, not whether pair associations were learned.
Corpus used only in verification; candidate extraction must be separately audited.
Preserving pairs can force some longer substrings; rigid graphs may remain unchanged.
